questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word to complete the sentence: The new market in Aba can ______ more than two hundred traders at a time.
questions.explanation: The sentence needs the correctly spelt verb meaning to provide space for people. The correct spelling is “accommodate”, which has double c and double m; the other forms are misspellings with a single c or a single m.

questions.q: Choose the correct form of the word in brackets to complete the sentence: The ______ (arrive) of the first textile machines changed life in the town.
questions.explanation: The blank requires a noun formed from “arrive”. “Arrival” is the standard noun, while “arriving” is a participle/gerund and does not fit naturally before “of the first textile machines”; “arrived” is a verb and “arriver” is not the intended noun.

questions.q: The new market supervisor, as well as the two security guards, ______ scheduled to meet the traders tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular “supervisor”. The phrase “as well as the two security guards” does not make the subject plural, so the singular verb “is” is required; the plural forms are wrongly attracted by the plural noun “guards”.

questions.q: By the time the durbar ended, the horsemen ______ their skills three times to the delight of visitors.
questions.explanation: The phrase “By the time the durbar ended” places the displaying before another past event, so the past perfect “had displayed” is needed. “Have displayed” is present perfect, “were displaying” is past continuous, and “display” is the base form.

questions.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as the “a” in “made”?
questions.explanation: The “a” in “made” has the same vowel sound as the “ai” in “rain”. “Pan” has a short vowel, while “mall” and “wash” have rounded vowel sounds.

questions.q: At the meeting, the chairperson asked members not to beat about the bush when discussing the new market levy. What did she mean?
options: repeat the same point many times
avoid speaking directly about the matter
questions.explanation: To beat about the bush is to avoid coming directly to the main point. It does not mean deciding quickly, repeating a point, or leaving a meeting.

questions.passage: Last term, Government Secondary School, Otukpo, introduced a rule that every senior student must take part in a compulsory evening study session from seven to nine, whether or not the student has a quiet place at home. The principal argued that the rule would raise performance in the West African examination. However, the rule ignores the reality of many students. Some live far away and travel by motorcycle along busy roads; ending at nine exposes them to danger. Others help in their parents' shops after school and use the morning for private reading. During the first week, more than forty students reached home after ten o'clock. A parent, Mrs Eze, said her daughter had stopped attending evening lessons because the family could not afford the transport for two trips. The students' council has suggested that the school provide supervised study only for those who choose it. This is reasonable. A rule should support learning without turning hardship into punishment.
questions.q: According to the passage, why did the principal introduce the compulsory evening study session?
options: to reduce the cost of transport for parents
to raise performance in the West African examination
to keep students away from their parents' shops
to prepare students for the students' council election
questions.explanation: The passage states that the principal argued the rule would raise performance in the West African examination. The other details are either effects noted by critics or matters not linked to the principal's reason.

questions.q: According to the passage, what happened during the first week of the new rule?
options: More than forty students reached home after ten o'clock.
Parents held a meeting at the town hall.
The school provided free transport for students.
questions.explanation: The passage reports that during the first week, more than forty students reached home after ten o'clock. Free transport and a town hall meeting are not mentioned; the parent's comment was about the cost of transport.

questions.q: According to the passage, what did the students' council suggest?
options: Supervised study should be provided only for students who choose it.
Evening study should begin at six o'clock.
Every student should pay a study fee.
The rule should be extended to junior students.
questions.explanation: The students' council suggested that the school provide supervised study only for those who choose it. Extending the rule, charging a study fee and changing the starting time are not proposed in the passage.

questions.q: Identify the word whose primary stress falls on a different syllable from that of the other three.
questions.explanation: Develop has its primary stress on the second syllable, while furniture, carpenter and calendar have primary stress on the first syllable. The difference is therefore one of stress placement, not spelling.

questions.q: If a speaker says "Ngozi bought the textbooks at the market yesterday" but needs to correct the claim that the textbooks were bought from a bookshop, which word should receive the emphatic stress?
questions.explanation: The contrast is between where the textbooks were bought: the claim says a bookshop, so the speaker stresses market to correct it. Stressing Ngozi, textbooks or yesterday would correct different kinds of information.

questions.q: Neither the goalkeeper nor the defenders ______ able to stop the free kick.
questions.explanation: In a neither ... nor construction, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, defenders, which is plural. The past context also calls for were, so the singular forms do not agree.

questions.q: The committee has not yet decided ______ to hold the inter-house sports in Awka or in Enugu.
questions.explanation: The correct structure is decide whether to do something, especially when alternatives are expressed with or. If is not used before to in this standard construction, and weather is a noun unrelated to choice.

questions.q: The elder's calm words helped to ______ the tension between the two families.
questions.explanation: Defuse means to reduce or calm a dangerous or tense situation, so it fits the elder's calming words. Diffuse means to spread out, refuse means to decline, and infuse means to fill or introduce something.

questions.q: Which word begins with the same consonant sound as the 'g' in 'ginger'?
questions.explanation: The g in ginger has a soft g sound, like the first sound in jump. Giant begins with that same soft g sound, while gate, goat and gum begin with the hard g sound heard in go.

questions.passage: When the Adeyemis packed their belongings into a borrowed lorry and left their crowded two-room apartment in Mushin for a small bungalow in Ikorodu, fourteen-year-old Simi expected the world to change at once. The new compound had a mango tree, a well and enough space for her mother to dry peppers without fighting for sun. Yet by the second week, the family was quarrelling over small things: who had used the last tin of milk, whose turn it was to fetch water, and why the landlord's nephew kept his radio loud at night. Mr Adeyemi, who had paid twelve thousand naira for the lorry and another twenty-five thousand for the rent advance, refused to join the quarrels. One evening, he gathered his wife and children under the mango tree and reminded them that a house becomes a home only when its people practise patience. Simi looked at the unopened cartons still stacked in the corridor and understood, at last, why her father had said nothing on the day they moved.
questions.q: What does Mr Adeyemi's statement that a house becomes a home only when its people practise patience suggest?
options: Patience is needed only while the family is unpacking its belongings.
Harmonious living depends more on how family members treat one another than on the building itself.
The new bungalow will remain uncomfortable until more furniture is bought.
Family members should avoid discussing their disagreements altogether.
questions.explanation: The statement contrasts a mere building with a home, which is made by the conduct of the people in it. It therefore stresses that tolerance among family members creates a settled home, not the physical house alone. The idea that patience is only for unpacking misses the father's broader lesson.

questions.q: What does Simi's final understanding reveal about her father's silence on the day they moved?
options: He did not know how the cartons should be arranged in the corridor.
He regretted paying for the lorry and the rent advance.
He hoped that the family would soon return to Mushin.
He had been allowing the family time to learn that settling down required tolerance.
questions.explanation: The passage says Mr Adeyemi later gathered the family and taught them about patience, and Simi then understood his earlier silence. This shows that he was not sulking about money or planning to return, but waiting for them to learn a lesson about living together. His silence was part of the lesson rather than ignorance about the cartons.

questions.q: What do the quarrels in the second week show about the Adeyemis' move?
options: The family had exhausted its money on milk and water.
The landlord's nephew alone caused every disagreement in the compound.
The novelty of the new compound did not remove the need for the family to adjust to one another.
Simi's mother preferred the crowded apartment in Mushin.
questions.explanation: The passage lists minor disputes after the family has settled in, showing that a better environment does not automatically create harmony. It therefore highlights the need for adjustment, not a shortage of milk or a wish to return to Mushin. The nephew's radio is only one of several small causes of friction.

questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'credible' as used in the sentence: The supervisor found the clerk's account of the missing money credible.
questions.explanation: Credible describes something that can be believed or accepted as true. The clerk's account was credible because the supervisor found it believable, not because it was necessarily detailed or confusing. Suspicious is the opposite of the intended meaning.

questions.q: Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to 'permissive' as used in the sentence: The matron's permissive approach to visiting hours encouraged indiscipline in the hostel.
questions.explanation: A permissive approach allows people considerable freedom, so its opposite is one that imposes limits. Restrictive describes an approach that controls or limits visiting hours. Flexible is closer to permissive in this context, while unconcerned describes lack of interest rather than strict regulation.

questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'derisive' as used in the sentence: The trader's derisive comments about the new market rules angered the chairman.
questions.explanation: Derisive language ridicules or mocks something, which explains why the chairman was angered. Helpful and respectful are positive qualities and do not fit comments that provoked anger. Confusing refers to lack of clarity, not ridicule.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word to complete the sentence: The ward councillor promised to present the residents' ______ to the local government chairman.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is grievances, the plural of grievance, meaning complaints or causes for complaint. The other forms either place the vowels in the wrong order or add an unnecessary syllable. In the sentence, the residents' complaints are what the councillor will present.

questions.q: Choose the correct form of the word in brackets to complete the sentence: The new librarian arranged the books so ______ (method) that the pupils found them easy to locate.
questions.explanation: The blank modifies the verb arranged, so an adverb is needed. Methodically means in an orderly or systematic way and fits the phrase so methodically that. Methodical is an adjective, method is a noun, and methodology is a noun meaning a system of methods.

questions.q: The list of candidates shortlisted for the scholarship ______ pasted on the notice board last Friday.
questions.explanation: The subject of the sentence is list, which is singular, and the verb must agree with it. The time marker last Friday also requires a simple past form, making was the correct choice. Were would wrongly agree with candidates rather than the head noun list.

questions.q: By the time Ngozi finished her project, her brother ______ the faulty generator.
questions.explanation: The repairing happened before another past action, Ngozi finished her project, so the earlier action takes the past perfect had repaired. The present forms has repaired, repairs, and is repairing do not fit the sequence of past events. The phrase by the time also signals that one past action was completed before another.

questions.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as the 'i' in 'bite'?
questions.explanation: The i in bite represents /aɪ/, and the first syllable of island is pronounced with /aɪ/. Mist has /ɪ/, meet has /iː/, and met has /e/.

questions.q: In the sentence 'Adaeze bought a new thermometer yesterday', which word should receive the emphatic stress if the speaker is correcting the impression that she bought it today?
questions.explanation: The speaker is correcting the idea that the purchase was made today, so the contrast falls on yesterday. Emphatic stress is placed on the word that supplies the correction.

questions.passage: When Hajara resumed as the only midwife at the clinic in Dange, she found that many pregnant women arrived only after several hours of labour. The long journey by motorcycle over sandy roads was not the only reason. Some families delayed because they believed the clinic charged heavily, although the fee for a normal delivery was only ₦2,000. Hajara began holding short talks after Friday prayers with the women's group. She showed them the clinic's price list, explained danger signs, and trained two volunteers to ride with expectant mothers on scheduled market days. At first, only a few women came. Six months later, however, the clinic recorded twenty-three deliveries in one month, more than double the previous record. The district officer praised the programme, but Hajara pointed to a less visible change: neighbours had begun to remind one another about antenatal appointments. She insisted that the trust built during the talks, not the new posters on the wall, had done the most to bring women to the clinic.
questions.q: Which detail best shows that Hajara's programme was successful?
options: The district officer praised the programme.
Two volunteers rode with mothers on market days.
Posters about antenatal care were placed on the wall.
The clinic recorded twenty-three deliveries in one month.
questions.explanation: The clearest evidence of success is the clinic recording twenty-three deliveries in one month, more than double its previous record. The posters and volunteer rides were means or details, while the district officer's praise is not as concrete a result.

questions.q: What did Hajara consider most responsible for the increased number of women attending the clinic?
options: The new posters on the wall
The trust built during her talks
The low fee for a normal delivery
The praise from the district officer
questions.explanation: Hajara insisted that the trust built during her talks, rather than the new posters, had done the most to bring women to the clinic. The passage mentions posters specifically to contrast them with that trust.

questions.q: The farmer advised that the seedlings ______ watered at dusk to reduce evaporation.
questions.explanation: After 'advised that', the verb in the that-clause takes the subjunctive form 'be watered', not a finite present or past form. 'Are', 'were' and 'will be' do not fit the required subjunctive construction.

questions.q: By the time the village head returned from the farm, the rain ______ for over an hour.
questions.explanation: The time clause 'By the time... returned' places the rain before that past moment, so the past perfect continuous 'had been falling' is needed for an action continuing up to then. Simple past or present forms do not show the earlier continuing action.

questions.q: The heavy rain prevented the farmers ______ harvesting the maize on time.
questions.explanation: The verb 'prevented' is followed by the preposition 'from' before an -ing form: prevented the farmers from harvesting. 'Against', 'to' and 'with' do not fit this fixed pattern.

questions.passage: When Musa returned to his farm in Kano after the first rain, he found that the ground had softened only at the surface. Beneath it, the earth was still hard, as though the dry season had refused to loosen its grip. He had borrowed ₦18,000 to buy maize seed and fertiliser, and every neighbour who passed his field asked why he had planted so early. Musa did not argue. He simply pointed to the dark clouds gathering over the hills and said that a farmer who waits until the rain is certain often plants when the season is already leaving. By August, his maize stood taller than that on the neighbouring farms, but he warned his nephew not to boast. 'The harvest is not counted in the field,' he said. 'It is counted in the barn.' The rain eventually came in heavy, uneven bursts, and some farmers who had delayed lost their seedlings to a short dry spell before they could take root.
questions.q: Why did Musa plant early despite his neighbours' questions?
options: He had borrowed money and wanted to repay it quickly.
He wanted his maize to grow taller than his neighbours' maize.
He was sure the rain would be heavy and regular.
He expected the rain and knew that delay could shorten the season.
questions.explanation: The passage shows Musa reading the clouds and warning that waiting for certain rain can make a farmer plant too late. It does not say he planted early merely to repay a loan, outgrow neighbours, or because he expected heavy and regular rain.

questions.q: What did Musa mean by 'The harvest is not counted in the field... It is counted in the barn'?
options: A promising crop is not a real success until it has been safely harvested and stored.
Farmers should count their crops before storing them.
Tall maize in the field always brings a large harvest.
The barn is a more important place than the field.
questions.explanation: Musa is saying that a crop still in the field may yet be lost; success is known only after harvest and safe storage. The warning is against boasting before the harvest, not about counting crops literally or about the barn being more important.

questions.q: The statement that the dry season had 'refused to loosen its grip' suggests that
options: Musa was unable to work on his farm.
the soil was too soft for planting.
the earth remained very dry beneath the surface.
the rainy season had ended completely.
questions.explanation: Because only the surface had softened while the earth beneath was still hard, 'refused to loosen its grip' describes the dry season's continuing hold on the deeper soil. It does not mean the rainy season had ended, since the first rain had come.

questions.q: Which word ends with the same final consonant sound as the 'th' in 'health'?
questions.explanation: The 'th' in 'health' is the voiceless /θ/ sound, and 'bath' ends with the same /θ/ sound. 'Bathe' and 'smooth' end with voiced /ð/, while 'boots' ends with /s/.

questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'apprehensive' as used in the sentence: The villagers were apprehensive about the dark clouds gathering over the hills.
questions.explanation: 'Apprehensive' means feeling uneasy or fearful about something, so 'anxious' is nearest in meaning. 'Indifferent' and 'confident' suggest the opposite feeling, while 'excited' does not carry the sense of worry.

questions.passage: In the quiet village of Gboko, after the last generator coughed and died, the night sky became a vast theatre. Ada and her younger brother, Emeka, lay on a mat outside their father's compound, their eyes fixed on the stars. The moon was a shy lantern, playing hide-and-seek behind the clouds. Every now and then, it slipped out and painted the roofs of the neighbours' houses with silver. The stars were scattered grains of rice on a black cloth, too many for anyone to count. A cool breeze whispered through the mango tree, and the children listened as their grandmother told stories of ancient travellers who used the stars to find their way. 'The sky is a big map,' she said, 'and those bright ones are the eyes of our ancestors watching us.' Emeka laughed, but he kept looking up, hoping to see a shooting star. For a moment, the whole village seemed to hold its breath, and the night was a calm sea with no waves.
questions.q: In the passage, the expression 'the moon was a shy lantern' is used to suggest that the moon
options: was extremely bright and steady throughout the night
was afraid of the children watching it
was as small as a lantern held by someone
was often hidden by clouds but appeared from time to time
questions.explanation: The metaphor and personification suggest that the moon was partly concealed and came out intermittently. It is not literally a lantern, nor is it afraid; the expression describes its appearance in the sky.

questions.q: The phrase 'the stars were scattered grains of rice on a black cloth' is an example of
questions.explanation: The phrase directly describes the stars as grains of rice without using 'like' or 'as', which makes it a metaphor. A simile would use a comparison word, and the expression does not exaggerate or give human qualities to the stars.

questions.q: In the passage, the verb 'were' in the sentence 'The stars were scattered grains of rice on a black cloth' agrees with the subject
questions.explanation: The subject of the sentence is 'The stars', which is plural, so the plural verb 'were' is correct. 'Grains of rice' is the complement, not the subject.

questions.q: When the bus finally reached Enugu after a long delay, the conductor told the passengers that the delay was a bitter pill to swallow. What did he mean?
options: The delay was an unpleasant fact they had to accept.
The delay was a medicine they had to take for their health.
The delay was a sweet experience they enjoyed.
The delay was caused by a quarrel among the passengers.
questions.explanation: 'A bitter pill to swallow' means an unpleasant situation that must be accepted. The other meanings take the idiom literally or misunderstand it as a quarrel.

questions.q: Choose the correct form of the word in brackets to complete the sentence: The team's ______ (succeed) in launching the rocket was celebrated throughout the school.
questions.explanation: The possessive 'team's' requires a noun, and 'success' is the noun form of 'succeed'. 'Succeed' is a verb, 'successful' an adjective, and 'successfully' an adverb.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word to complete the sentence: The astronomer's ______ of the data was careful and accurate.
questions.explanation: 'Analysis' is the correct noun meaning a detailed examination. 'Analyse' is the verb, and the other spellings are incorrect.

questions.q: By the time the clouds cleared, the astronomy club ______ the planet through the telescope.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had observed' is needed for an action completed before another past action ('cleared'). 'Has' and 'have' are present perfect, and 'observes' is simple present.

questions.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as the 'i' in 'night'?
questions.explanation: 'Night' and 'light' both contain the /aɪ/ diphthong. 'Sit' and 'bit' have /ɪ/, while 'neat' has /iː/.

questions.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as the 'o' in 'moon'?
questions.explanation: 'Moon' and 'soon' both have the long /uː/ vowel. 'Book' has /ʊ/, while 'cost' and 'lot' have /ɒ/.

questions.passage: When Nneka joined the sanitation club at Government Secondary School, Owerri, she expected only sweeping and lectures. One afternoon, while cleaning a locked store behind the science block, she found a dusty notebook under a broken microscope. Its cover bore the name 'Mr Eze' and the date 1998. Inside were neat sketches of a small water filter made from a clay pot, charcoal, sand and gravel, with notes on how it once supplied clean water to the school clinic. Nneka took the notebook to the principal, who recognised it as the work of a retired science teacher. The school had abandoned the filter after a pipe was installed, but the pipe had broken three months earlier. With Mr Eze's sketches and a grant of ₦45,000 from an old students' association, Nneka's club rebuilt the filter. By the following term, the clinic no longer bought bottled water, saving ₦6,000 every month. Nneka had gone looking for rubbish; she found a solution instead.
questions.q: What did Nneka expect when she joined the sanitation club?
options: She expected only sweeping and lectures.
She expected to rebuild a water filter.
She expected to meet Mr Eze.
She expected to receive a grant of ₦45,000.
questions.explanation: The passage says Nneka expected only sweeping and lectures when she joined the club. Rebuilding the filter and the ₦45,000 grant came later as a result of her unexpected discovery.

questions.q: What unexpected discovery did Nneka make behind the science block?
options: Bottled water stored for the school clinic.
A dusty notebook containing sketches of a water filter.
A broken pipe that had supplied the school clinic.
A grant of ₦45,000 from old students.
questions.explanation: The passage states that she found a dusty notebook under a broken microscope, and the notebook contained neat sketches of a small water filter. The broken pipe is mentioned as the reason the old filter was abandoned, not as the object she discovered.

questions.passage: When Nneka joined the sanitation club at Government Secondary School, Owerri, she expected only sweeping and lectures. One afternoon, while cleaning a locked store behind the science block, she found a dusty notebook under a broken microscope. Its cover bore the name 'Mr Eze' and the date 1998. Inside were neat sketches of a small water filter made from a clay pot, charcoal, sand and gravel, with notes on how it once supplied clean water to the school clinic. Nneka took the notebook to the principal, who recognised it as the work of a retired science teacher. The school had abandoned the filter after a pipe was installed, but the pipe had broken three months earlier. With Mr Eze's sketches and a grant of ₦45,000 from an old students' association, Nneka's club rebuilt the filter. By the following term, the clinic no longer bought bottled water, saving ₦6,000 every month. Nneka had gone looking for rubbish; she found a solution instead.
questions.q: Which detail best shows that the rebuilt filter helped the school financially?
options: The clinic stopped buying bottled water and saved ₦6,000 every month.
The old students' association provided a grant of ₦45,000.
Nneka's club cleaned a locked store behind the science block.
The school abandoned the filter after a pipe was installed.
questions.explanation: Saving ₦6,000 monthly by no longer buying bottled water is direct evidence of financial benefit. The grant helped fund the rebuilding, but it was a cost rather than proof of the filter's later savings.

questions.q: Which of the following words has its primary stress on the third syllable?
questions.explanation: The word magazine has three syllables, and its primary stress falls on the third syllable. Beautiful carries primary stress on the first syllable, develop on the second, and important on the second.

questions.q: In the sentence 'Amina travelled to Kaduna by bus on Tuesday', which word should receive emphatic stress to correct the claim that she travelled by train?
questions.explanation: The contrast is between travelling by bus and the mistaken claim that the journey was by train, so the word bus should be stressed. Stressing Amina, Kaduna or Tuesday would correct a different kind of mistaken detail.

questions.q: No sooner had the pupils settled down ______ the fire alarm rang.
questions.explanation: The fixed correlative construction is 'no sooner ... than', which links the two past events. 'When', 'then' and 'that' do not complete this construction correctly.

questions.q: If the trader ______ the yams in a dry store, they would not have rotted.
questions.explanation: This is a third conditional sentence about a past situation that did not happen, so the if-clause needs the past perfect 'had kept'. The main clause 'would not have rotted' shows that a past unreal condition is required.

questions.q: The new road, together with the street lights, ______ almost completed.
questions.explanation: The subject of the sentence is 'the new road', which is singular; the phrase 'together with the street lights' does not change the number of the subject. Therefore the singular verb 'is' agrees with it.

questions.q: Which word ends with the same final consonant sound as the 's' in 'chairs'?
questions.explanation: The 's' in chairs is pronounced like 'z', and lives also ends with the 'z' sound. Caps, makes and kites end with an 's' sound rather than the required 'z' sound.

questions.q: Had the boatman in Brass not shouted a warning, the fishermen would have steered straight into the storm. What does the sentence imply?
options: The fishermen ignored the boatman and entered the storm.
The boatman's warning stopped the fishermen from steering into the storm.
The boatman shouted only after the fishermen had reached the storm.
The boatman himself steered the boat away from the storm.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses a past unreal conditional to show what would have happened if the warning had not been given. Since the fishermen did not steer into the storm, the warning must have prevented them from doing so. The statement does not say that the boatman steered the boat himself.

questions.q: When the librarian in Abeokuta said that the new novel had more cover than content, she meant that the novel ______.
options: looked substantial but lacked real depth
contained more pages than the library expected
dealt mainly with farming and fishing
questions.explanation: The expression contrasts outward appearance with inner substance. Saying a book has more cover than content means it appears impressive but lacks real meaning or depth. It does not refer mainly to the beauty of the cover or the number of pages.

questions.q: Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to transparent as used in the sentence: The lecturer's explanation was transparent to the new students at Lokoja.
questions.explanation: Here transparent means clear and easy to understand, so the opposite is obscure, meaning unclear. Obvious is close in meaning to clear, not opposite, while detailed and polite do not contrast with transparent.

questions.q: Choose the correct form of the word in brackets to complete the sentence: The ______ (maintain) of the fishing boat's engine costs Bassey a great deal every season.
questions.explanation: The noun formed from maintain is maintenance, spelt m-a-i-n-t-e-n-a-n-c-e. The other forms insert or omit letters incorrectly. The completed sentence correctly refers to the cost of keeping the engine in good condition.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word to complete the sentence: The community contributed generously to the ______ of the town library in Oyo.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is renovation, from the verb renovate. The other forms misspell the middle syllable of the word. In the sentence, renovation means the repair and improvement of the library building.
